correctness.rationale: For each base b, every eligible two-digit state 1<=n<b² with r=n mod b!=0 is a vertex of the exact successor functional graph; its cycles are precisely primitive propagating cycles, without missing any eligible states. For each integer b=2..1230, complete traversal of all states proves existence at the stated first bases and nonexistence at every smaller base. Original C++ includes two different exhaustive methods (three-color path tracing and indegree peeling) and explicit witness rows. An independently written optimized C++ DFS fully traversed 620,288,590 eligible states over all 1229 bases and reproduced every one of the 19 values, not just preselected seeds. The maximum is 1230 at length20. It is a bounded finite assertion; no infinite-length conjecture is being inferred.

evidence: Primary Theorem 2.7 propagates an existing cycle along arithmetic progressions of larger bases; Remark 2.13 merely says for all l<=20 some b<=1230 supports a propagating l-cycle.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existence/positive-density theorems for all l do not establish least base beta(l). Propagation beyond a seed is inapplicable for ruling out all smaller bases; full exhaustion is necessary.

value.rationale: The smallest-base spectrum for a canonical, explicitly posed digit-dynamics problem is a meaningful finite complete classification: the 19 exact minima reveal sharp nonmonotonicity (beta(17)=1120, beta(18)=96) and prove the original uniform existence cutoff 1230 is optimal. Finite exhaustive mathematics is intrinsically valuable here because the invariant concerns a fixed natural cutoff and was explicitly posed in prior work.

limitations: All b up to 1230 were exhausted; this proves only least bases for cycle lengths 2..20 because positive witnesses occur within that range.
No claim about higher length, polynomial growth of beta(l), or cycles outside the propagating restriction.
